$comment: CfxLua runtime functions, tagged with the realm each is legal in. Hand-authored, because most are NOT in natives_cfx.json: that database holds game natives, while the scheduler, event, resource and type-construction functions are provided by the CfxLua runtime itself. The plan calls for them to live in their own realm-tagged list. 'shared' means FiveM provides the function on both the client and the server VM; 'client' and 'server' mean the other realm would raise or silently no-op. Sources: runtime.fivem.net/docs/scripting-reference and the CfxLua runtime manual. The tail of the client list is natives the LIVE HARNESS (test/live) uses that cis_libs itself does not, so they never reach the generated natives.json; without them the linter reports every one as an undefined global. A name that IS in natives_cfx.json does not belong here at all and its realm comes from that file's apiset: SetEntityRoutingBucket was listed as client-only and was wrong, which made the realm check report a server call to it as a violation when the server setter is exactly what it exists for. This file is read after natives.json and overwrites it, so tools/natives/realm-guard.js fails check-realms and gen-natives on any row whose realm differs from the published one, except Wait, GetGameTimer and GetPlayerName, which CfxLua provides on both VMs. Natives only the harness touches belong in the harness list in tools/gen-luacheck.js, not here.
